Living Well / Resource directory

Find and keep the right document

Start with life

What would be useful?

Be able to open the correct, complete source when it matters.

The simpler starting point: An understandable filename and a short index may solve the problem. A clear photograph can be sufficient for an ordinary notice.

Finish when: Locate the saved copy on the device where it is needed and verify its completeness against the original.

Choose by fit

Different tools, different jobs.

These are editorial comparisons based on public descriptions, not a ranking from hands-on tests. Choose one suitable route; using every option is not the goal.

Google Drive: scan a document

Consider it when: You already use Drive and need to capture a small paper document.

Check first: Check storage, sharing, cropping, and the correct account.

Access: Free instructions; the mobile workflow needs a compatible device, Drive access, and available account storage.

Open Google Drive: scan a document · Full context and source

NAPS2: scan and arrange pages

Consider it when: You use a desktop scanner or need to arrange multiple pages.

Check first: Inspect the saved images as well as searchable text.

Access: Free open-source software for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Scanning requires compatible hardware and drivers.

Open NAPS2: scan and arrange pages · Full context and source

ZoteroBib: a one-off bibliography

Consider it when: You need a short source list rather than a full document archive.

Check first: Check the citation against the source; formatted references are not evidence checks.

Access: Free browser service without an account or installation. It uses browser storage; sharing a saved version uploads that version.

Open ZoteroBib: a one-off bibliography · Full context and source

Zotero

Consider it when: You need an ongoing library of sources for writing and research.

Check first: Distinguish bibliographic records from access to the full text.

Access: The core research application is free. Additional hosted file storage is an optional paid service.

Explore Zotero · Full context and source

Google Takeout: keep an export

Consider it when: The information you need sits inside a Google account.

Check first: Check what the export includes and how you will protect the downloaded copy.

Access: Free instructions; exporting requires access to the relevant account and space to receive and store the files.

Open Google Takeout: keep an export · Full context and source

From choice to use

Keep the human purpose visible.

Separate capture from interpretation

First make the source readable and findable. A generated explanation cannot repair a missing page or identify the authoritative version by confidence alone.

Test retrieval

Close the app. Search using words you would naturally remember, open the result, and confirm the subject and version. Test offline access only when you genuinely need it.

Respect consequential originals

This path does not decide retention rules for legal, financial, or medical records. Keep those requirements separate from the convenience of a scan.
